draft.title: Circulatory and respiratory systems
card: Lungs
The lungs take in oxygen from the air we breathe in. They also remove carbon dioxide, which leaves the body when we breathe out.
Heart
The heart is a muscle that pumps blood around the body. The blood moves through tubes called blood vessels.
Blood
Blood picks up oxygen in the lungs and carries it to every cell. It also carries nutrients from digestion to every cell.
Cells
Cells use oxygen and nutrients to get energy, and they make carbon dioxide. Blood carries the carbon dioxide back to the lungs to be breathed out.
draft.remember: The lungs swap gases with the blood, and the heart pumps the blood to and from every cell.

a.q: Which job does the heart do in the body?
opts: Pumps blood through the blood vessels
Takes oxygen in from the air we breathe
Removes carbon dioxide from the body
Breaks food down into small nutrients
a.why: The heart is a muscle that pumps blood through the blood vessels. Taking in oxygen and removing carbon dioxide is the job of the lungs, so that option is tempting but wrong.
a.clue: Think about which organ is a muscle that moves blood.

b.q: Kai runs hard and his muscle cells use more oxygen. How does the oxygen reach his muscle cells?
opts: The blood carries it from the lungs to the cells
The lungs pass it straight into the muscle cells
The heart makes it and sends it to the cells
The blood vessels make it as the blood moves
b.why: Oxygen enters the blood in the lungs, and the heart pumps that blood through blood vessels to every cell. The lungs do not pass oxygen straight to muscles, because blood is the carrier.
b.clue: Something has to carry the oxygen from the lungs to the cells.
